coaching.headline: The duo ran riot. We turned it into a strong win.
coaching.team: Drongo and Phase had a hell of a game: lethal carry, deathless support, and a win without dragging it into a coin flip. The early Fangtooth went against us, but we took the next two and finished ahead on towers. Trading Fangtooth for their Mini Prime kept our objective progress moving. Keep that confidence and make the next take-or-reset call together.

focus.title: Make the next call obvious
focus.evidence: Five favorable kill clusters are recorded; three had a major objective or structure follow within 90 seconds. The other two do not establish that an objective was safely available. Health, wave position and travel time are not captured.
focus.action: After the next won fight, name one reachable objective or tower, check the wave and surviving threats, then call take or reset. Everyone should hear the decision before splitting up.

perPlayer.dba6b55f-c3aa-499a-aa76-266f3f9610d5: Drongo was the fucking problem they never solved. Huge damage, repeated kills on their duo, barely any time dead. Keep that balance. When Greystone comes into range, hit him from beside the team instead of spending the escape to reach Kira; once the threat is gone and a wave arrives, put those expensive bullets into the tower. This game earned confidence, not a license to dive everything.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Phase stayed alive and contributed to nearly every kill. Deathless with that much involvement is a damn good support game. Keep enabling the damage dealer. When Drongo commits to a target he can actually hit, match Hyperflux to that shooting window; if he needs pulling out, call it before yanking him away from the kill. Make the partnership deliberate.
perPlayer.8d51b81b-7acf-4747-8b3a-2a225758fb5e: Khaimera brought the team's biggest objective damage contribution. Keep giving the squad something to collect beyond kills. Before starting the next major objective, call whether the plan is to finish it or turn on Greystone if he approaches, and get Drongo's answer. Half the team burning the monster while the other half starts a different fight is how a comfortable game becomes bullshit.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Belica's farm was strong, but Argus got both her deaths, including one just before their first Fangtooth. That is the sequence worth tightening. When the next objective is coming up, clear from safety and keep Seismic Assault available if Argus can threaten the route. Call a delayed rotation instead of forcing a trade to leave lane. Keep the income; arrive ready to use it.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Steel does not need to cosplay Drongo on the damage chart. He led our mitigation and kept his deaths down. With this carry ahead, the next grouped push needs a bodyguard: when Greystone or Scarlett steps toward Drongo, use the stun to stop that threat before chasing their backline. Let the wave take tower shots. Keep the durability, and make it buy the carry room to work.

13.9.call: We won the kill sequence and then took Fangtooth while they took Mini Prime. Keep the trade in perspective. The next call is whether the nearby lane and remaining health allow a tower, not an automatic sprint to the other pit.

19.7.call: A clean kill sequence was followed by towers and another Fangtooth. That is the sequence to repeat: agree on the reachable prize and finish it before looking for another fight.

21.9.call: Drongo and Khaimera died in the final favorable exchange, then another enemy tower fell. When the main carry is down, check the wave and surviving defenders before extending; the earlier lead does not make every push free.

matchup: Greystone's healing made him the persistent front-line problem; Kira and Ikra built damage, not armor.
Focus the target Drongo can reach safely, not their already-struggling carry.
build: Demolisher's bonus-armor penetration had little item armor to work against: the last slot is debatable, not wasted.
eternal: Weald rewards damaging low-health heroes, matching the finishing role.
In a draft where sustained trading matters more, Taproot trades Wind-Rider's attack-speed boost for on-hit healing.
Phase's sustain supports keeping the aggressive option here.
augment: Bring The Boom splashes nearby enemies when Greystone or Scarlett is the reachable target.
Splash hits are not measured, so keep it for that plan without crediting it for kills.
crest: Pacifier gives Drongo finishing pressure and a way to reposition against Greystone.
Using the dash forward costs the immediate escape; kills do not prove its resets were decisive.
improvement: Tainted Rounds is worth comparing with Demolisher when Greystone's healing protects Drongo's own target.
Teammates owning anti-heal does not guarantee it lands on that target at the right time.
Keep Demolisher if armor becomes the bigger problem; this win does not prove a compulsory swap.

matchup: Greystone and Scarlett join Kira and Ikra as threats when fights group.
Astral Catalyst still punishes shielded teammates like Steel or Belica using Soulbearer.
build: A workable damage-and-sustain package, but its attack-based value needs safe chances to attack.
The deathless result does not show how often those chances came.
eternal: Exarch turns healing into attack speed and magical on-hit damage for a linked Drongo.
Revelation is a draft alternative to Preservation, trading personal sustain for more frequent basic abilities.
Zero deaths does not prove Preservation was unnecessary.
augment: Keep Psychic Support for longer exchanges; it keeps Drongo supplied with mana.
Swap only for an identified problem, not because another augment is more popular.
crest: Tranquility heals and briefly mitigates damage when Greystone or Scarlett reaches the group.
Ward totals do not show whether the right approach was covered.
improvement: If Phase cannot safely attack often, Marshal in Prophecy's slot shifts value from her on-hit damage to allies' attack speed.
If immobilization is denying Drongo his shooting time, Enra's Blessing offers a conditional shield for affected allies instead.
Keep Tainted Scepter when Phase can reliably apply its healing reduction to the enemy the team is focusing.

matchup: Greystone healed a lot and Scarlett's Mutilator pressures a health-stacking Khaimera.
Reaching gank targets is useful, but surviving the enemy bruisers matters once Khaimera commits.
build: Basilisk still helps against base armor and also helps Drongo on the same target.
eternal: Immaculate only reduces damage while health is high, not across a whole brawl.
Prima Donna is an aggressive draft alternative that also raises damage received, not a free upgrade.
augment: Keep Feral Ambush: the longer leap helps reach a called gank target.
Its value is access, not permission to engage beyond what the team can follow.
crest: Iceskorn Talons helps both Khaimera and Drongo when they fight inside its zone.
It is a positional benefit, not a permanent team buff.
improvement: Keep the sustained-fight package if Khaimera can stay on the same target with Drongo.
Sky Splitter over Basilisk adds attack speed, lifesteal and current-health damage, losing health, haste and shared armor reduction.
Against Greystone, anti-heal counts only if someone applies it during the duel.

matchup: Argus accounted for both recorded deaths, a matchup to examine, not proof of how they happened.
Belica's ultimate rewards missing mana, so Azure Core's mana pool and shield complicate burst.
build: Noxia needs a separate ability after the mark: Seismic Assault into Void Bomb does it.
Only two completed items are listed, so a missing third is not itself a mistake.
eternal: Keep Bottomless Vial when the lane plan includes personally securing River Buffs.
Philosopher is the draft alternative for steadier income without that requirement.
augment: Keep Combat Veteran if farming and rotating is the plan; the farm total is not its credit alone.
A damage augment next draft trades those benefits, not a retroactive fix for the Argus deaths.
crest: Soulbearer is Belica's defensive tool against Argus and incoming bruisers.
Ikra's Astral Catalyst hits that shield harder, so it is protection, not guaranteed safety.
improvement: If Belica survives the first exchange but lacks finishing damage, Wraith Leggings adds penetration against low-health targets.
If Argus burst prevents her from completing the exchange, weigh a defensive purchase before more offense.
The deciding evidence is whether survival or damage limits the next fight, not finishing the common core.

matchup: Scarlett's items pressure health and armor, and she earned both kills on Steel.
Argus and Ikra mean this is not only a physical-defense problem; the record does not isolate the deaths' cause.
build: Both items give physical armor for the bruiser matchup.
Tainted Guard's anti-heal hits Greystone only when he basic attacks Steel.
Infernum's armor interaction does not stop armor protecting Steel from her other physical damage.
eternal: This setup supports recovering between lane trades and growing sturdier.
Festering Wounds is a draft alternative to Regenerative Tissue: anti-heal through immobilization, no need to be attacked first.
augment: Keep Heavy Metal: it lets a defensive build still threaten nearby enemies.
Neither the low objective damage nor this win shows an offensive replacement is needed.
crest: Razorback fits committed damage from Scarlett or Greystone, used when it is actually coming into Steel.
It cannot force them to attack Steel instead of Drongo.
improvement: Keep Tainted Guard when its anti-heal is useful; don't drop all armor just because Scarlett has Infernum.
Flux Matrix is a next-slot option if Argus and Ikra become the limiting threats, giving up physical defense.

synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

loadout.text: Empowered Cindara leaves behind a rupture that erupts after 0.5s. The eruption deals 20 (+4 per Level) (+25%) Damage to Enemies and Slows by 40% for 1.25s.
loadout.plain: When an outer-edge Ashen Vow hit empowers your next Cindara, that lantern slam also leaves a rupture that erupts and slows. It gives your Ashen Vow into Cindara combo a second hit and makes it hard to walk out of.

loadout.text: Attacks and abilities against Enemy Heroes apply a stack of Rust for 5s. Each stack shreds 2% (+0.2% per Level) Physical Armor and Magical Armor, stacking up to 4 times. Gain 75% of the Armors shredded.

loadout.name: Patina
loadout.text: Gain a 30 (+14 per level) Shield when not taking damage for 10s. Gain 4% Movement Speed while the shield holds.
loadout.plain: A small shield and some move speed come back after you go untouched for 10s. Mostly a lane and roaming comfort piece; it softens the first poke before you dash in with First Intent.

loadout.name: Fracture
loadout.text: Deal 4% (+0.2% per level) more damage against targets with maximum stacks of Rust.
loadout.plain: Extra damage on anyone carrying max Rust from Knell. Since Scarlett chains stabs, slams and Cindara swings, she reaches max stacks fast, so this is a steady bonus through every extended trade.

loadout.name: Volcaic Slam
loadout.text: Empowered Cindara leaves behind a rupture that erupts after 0.5s. The eruption deals 20 (+4 per Level) (+25%) Damage to Enemies and Slows by 40% for 1.25s.
loadout.plain: When an outer-edge Ashen Vow hit empowers your next Cindara, that lantern slam also leaves a rupture that erupts and slows. It gives your Ashen Vow into Cindara combo a second hit and makes it hard to walk out of.

loadout.name: Knell
loadout.text: Attacks and abilities against Enemy Heroes apply a stack of Rust for 5s. Each stack shreds 2% (+0.2% per Level) Physical Armor and Magical Armor, stacking up to 4 times. Gain 75% of the Armors shredded.
loadout.plain: Every Cindara swing and ability on a hero adds Rust, cutting their armor and adding some to yours. Your fast stab and slam combos hit max Rust quickly, so longer trades against bruisers and tanks swing your way.

loadout.name: Patina
loadout.text: Gain a 30 (+14 per level) Shield when not taking damage for 10s. Gain 4% Movement Speed while the shield holds.
loadout.plain: A small shield and some move speed come back after you go untouched for 10s. Mostly a lane and roaming comfort piece; it softens the first poke before you dash in with First Intent.

loadout.name: Fracture
loadout.text: Deal 4% (+0.2% per level) more damage against targets with maximum stacks of Rust.
loadout.plain: Extra damage on anyone carrying max Rust from Knell. Since Scarlett chains stabs, slams and Cindara swings, she reaches max stacks fast, so this is a steady bonus through every extended trade.

loadout.name: Judgement
loadout.text: Thunder Cleaver:  Deal 70 (+40%) Damage in an area around you. On Hero hit, Heal (+30%) (+8%). Subsequent Hero hits Heal for 50% effectiveness.
loadout.plain: An area hit around you that heals you when it lands on heroes. Fire it in the middle of an Ashen Vow spin or right after Swan Song lands you in a group, for burst plus a heal.
